question: Indicate which of the following deficits leads to a glycogenosis:
reasoning_chain: CHAIN: Glucose 6-phosphatase -> inability to convert glucose-6-phosphate to glucose -> accumulation of glucose-6-phosphate -> glycogenosis -> 95% CHAIN: Fructose 1,6-bisphosphatase -> inability to convert fructose 1,6-bisphosphate to fructose 6-phosphate -> disruption in gluconeogenesis -> accumulation of substrates -> glycogenosis -> 95%
analysis: Deficits in enzymes involved in glycogen metabolism can lead to glycogen storage diseases (glycogenosis). Among the options provided, the deficiency of Glucose 6-phosphatase is associated with a glycogenosis known as Von Gierke disease (Type I glycogen storage disease). This enzyme is crucial for the final step in both glycogenolysis and gluconeogenesis.
